newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X shares stopped on Toronto exchange.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X shares stopped on Toronto exchange.

text.p: Shares in Canadian gold prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd have stopped trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange, traders said on Thursday.
The stock was up 0.23 at 3.43 on 5.02 million shares before trading was halted.
"Bre-X is inhibited for now. They are looking at the (computer trading) system...they don't want any problems with the overall system," said TSE spokeswoman Jane Wong.
She did not know when trading in Bre-X would resume.
The stock continued to trade on Nasdaq where the company's shares were up 3/16 at 2-1/2 on 2.1 million shares.
Trading was also unhampered on the Montreal Exchange where Bre-X gained 0.30 to 3.45 on 642,000 shares.

It was the third time this week that the TSE stopped trading in the volatile junior mining stock. Heavy order volumes and technical problems overwhelmed the exchange's 20-year-old trading system on Wednesday, forcing the TSE to shut down trading in Bre-X.
Bre-X shares have been volatile recently due to doubts over the size and viability of its Busang gold discovery in Indonesia.
